text:
incident-bot: [P1] GeoDNS anomalies detected — elevated SERVFAILs from Cloudflare resolvers for eu-west prefixes. Automated probes showing inconsistent propagation. Pager routed to #incidents and paging oncall-net.

oncall-net: I’m on it. jumping in, will triage connectivity + DNS path.

maria: seeing lots of SERVFAIL from 1.1.1.1 and 2606:4700:4700::1111 when querying for app-eu.redwood.ai A records. dig output:```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @1.1.1.1 app-eu.redwood.ai A +noall +answer
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
```

aj: Route53 health checks for the eu targets look OK from AWS side, but our GeoDNS service logs show repeated NXDOMAIN/SERVFAILs when proxying Cloudflare answers. Seems like external resolver layer failing to return cached answers intermittently.

support-esc: we’ve got 23 customer tickets in EU mentioning 502/timeout on features that hit the API. Escalated to SEs, getting customer org IDs now.

ops-lead: quick mitigation plan: 1) reduce GeoDNS TTL to 30s to speed up new answers, 2) temporarily bias weights to Route53-only for eu-west while CF is flaky, 3) fire a ticket with Cloudflare support and attach dig traces. Any objections? :thumbsup:

oncall-net: agree. starting with step 2 to minimize impact. running command to force weights.

oncall-net: ```
# force route53 for eu-west
redwood geodns update --region eu-west --provider route53 --weight 100 --provider cloudflare --weight 0
```

ops-lead: applied by oncall-net. confirming via geodns status:```
{ region: "eu-west", providers: [{name:"route53", weight:100}, {name:"cloudflare", weight:0}], ttl: 300 }
```

maria: starting TTL change to 30s now so resolvers re-query quickly:```
redwood geodns set-ttl --region eu-west --ttl 30
```

aj: note — lowering TTL will cause a short spike in DNS queries. autoscaling on the DNS control plane is ok.

eng-aws: pulled additional resolver logs from AWS vantage — Route53 answers are steady, propagation to edge seems fine. This looks like Cloudflare resolver fleet partially returning SERVFAIL for our zone.

maria: filed Cloudflare ticket with traces and sample dig outputs, ticket #CF-8421. Asked for escalation to engineering.

support-esc: posting customer impact summary to ops channel and CS: ~23 tickets, mostly EU SaaS customers, degraded read-only API and embed fetches. No major data loss.

ops-lead: enabling fail-open fallback: if GeoDNS provider returns SERVFAIL, clients will be routed to Route53 by policy. Pushing that config now.

oncall-net: pushed fallback rule. Verifying with probes. probe output (post-change):```
> probe eu-west -> resolver 1.1.1.1 -> got A 52.15.32.10 (route53) in 120ms
> probe eu-west -> resolver 8.8.8.8 -> got A 52.15.32.10 (route53) in 95ms
```

aj: synthetic traffic shows 95% of EU requests now successfully resolving to Route53-backed IPs. Error rate dropped from 14% -> 1.2% over the last 10m.

maria: rolling TTL back to 300 now once propagation stabilizes? recommend wait 15m to ensure resolver caches have route53 answers before raising TTL.

ops-lead: agreed. leave TTL low for 15m, monitor. cloudflare ticket updates?

maria: CF replied: investigating an internal resolver cluster causing intermittent SERVFAILs for certain zones. They repro'd with our traces and marked as Sev2. No ETA yet.

support-esc: CS sent proactively templated message to impacted customers linking status.redwood.ai and noting mitigation underway.

kevin: taking second shift handoff in 20m. can someone write a quick summary + actions done for my rotation?

ops-lead: summary for handoff -> short string you can paste: "GeoDNS provider (Cloudflare) experienced intermittent SERVFAILs for eu-west; we shifted geodns weights to Route53 only, lowered TTL to 30s, enabled provider-fallback policy; customer-facing impact reduced from 14% err to ~1.2%. Cloudflare ticket #CF-8421 opened; monitoring for recovery. Next steps: revert weights and TTL when CF confirms fix and metrics stable for >= 30m."

oncall-net: leaving monitoring alarms on. alert thresholds: dns_err_rate > 3% for 5m -> page oncall-net. probes still running every 30s.

aj: creating post-incident notes in #postmortems after we confirm root cause with Cloudflare. include dig/sec traces, TTL timeline, mitigation commands used.

ops-lead: thanks all. kevin — taking handoff at 3332101500. I’ll update the incident channel topic and add the CF ticket link. :white_check_mark:

kevin: got it — I’ll keep watch and coordinate with CF. ping me if anything spikes.

incident-bot: Incident P1 -> state changed to MONITORING. Handler: kevin. Duration so far: ~5m.
